name: amojs
description: HTML syntax highlighting and IntelliSense inside AmoJS html`` templates, plus build and eject commands.
comment:main: No "type": "module" on purpose — VS Code require()s the extension entry, so the bundle is CommonJS.
comment:activation: onLanguage is required: commands activate the extension by themselves, but diagnostics must be running BEFORE the user does anything, so the extension has to wake when a JS/TS file opens. Grammars and snippets are declarative and need no activation at all.

amojs.cli.path.markdownDescription: How to invoke the AmoJS CLI. Leave as `amo` when it is on your PATH; otherwise give an absolute path, or something like `pnpm amo`.

enumDescriptions: Compile pages to strings for rendering per request on node; islands/ is built for the browser in the same run.
Render pages under src/pages/ to static .html at build time; islands/ is built for the browser in the same run.
amojs.build.mode.markdownDescription: Which mode `amo build` runs in. `ssr` and `ssg` also compile `src/islands/` for the browser automatically.

amojs.build.srcDir.description: Source directory passed to `amo build` / `amo eject`, relative to the workspace folder.

amojs.build.outDir.description: Output directory passed to `amo build`, relative to the workspace folder.

amojs.eject.outDir.description: Output directory passed to `amo eject`, relative to the workspace folder.

amojs.eject.runtimeDir.description: Directory name the ejected runtime is written into, inside the eject output.

comment:deps: @amojs.dev/compiler is a devDependency, not a dependency, because esbuild BUNDLES it into dist/extension.js — the shipped .vsix carries no node_modules.
comment:vsce: vsce is run through npx, not installed: it pulls keytar and vsce-sign, native modules that need build scripts and are only ever needed at release time.
